1) We propose a general method to combine imitation and reinforcement learning for visuomotor control, 2) We show that our method can solve contact-rich tasks that neither the reinforcement nor the imitation learning can solve alone, 3) We show that the resulting policies can be transferred to the real robot with zero-shot transfer
our method is able to learn to perform diverse contact-rich tasks that neither reinforcement nor imitation learning methods could solve alone.
we can solve a wide range robot manipulation tasks with a deep reinforcement and imitation learning approach.

the problem of learning diverse visuomotor skills for robot manipulation.
how to learn diverse visuomotor skills with a single policy.
the problem of how a robot learns diverse visuomotor skills from demonstration data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach can solve contact rich manipulation tasks that neither imitation learning, reinforcement learning nor sim2real methods can do alone.
the proposed approach can be used as a general-purpose learning framework for a wide variety of robot tasks.
our method is a general and effective approach to learning diverse visuomotor skills.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that a general deep learning approach can learn diverse visuomotor skills from demonstrations, which can be applied to a large range of tasks, such as pushing, grasping, and pouring, with a single model.
the combination of reinforcement learning and imitation learning can solve diverse visuomotor skills that are hard to solve by either method alone.
our approach can learn to solve a diverse range of tasks with only a small amount of human demonstration data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
reinforcement learning can be a powerful tool to learn diverse and complex visuomotor skills from raw visual inputs.
reinforcement learning can learn diverse manipulation skills by leveraging demonstration data and can generalize to real-world tasks with minimal fine-tuning.

a combination of reinforcement and imitation learning can learn a wide variety of tasks that neither method can learn alone, and that the resulting policies can generalize across sim-to-real and across visual and dynamics domains.
